OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (territorial extension to Gibraltar)
Agreement between the UK and the EU on Trade and Cooperation (relevant provisions applicable to Gibraltar)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the jurisdiction of organization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for parties to the Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all partners and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, UK and Gibraltar financial sanctions screening of all partners, beneficial owners and authorized signatories; screening against GFSC sanctions list, UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and HM Treasury sanctions list; enhanced due diligence required for any PEP; adverse media and negative news checks; re-screening at engagement commencement and annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies Registry Gibraltar – Official Portal (Government of Gibraltar, Registrar of Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or transliterated into the Latin alphabet; an English translation must be provided for foreign script names. The name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' for a Gibraltar limited partnership. Names must not mislead or contravene public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name under the Limited Partnerships Act 2014 due to unacceptable similarity, misleading nature or prohibited token, the applicant may submit a written internal administrative review to the Registrar within 14 days of rejection, specifying statutory grounds and evidence of distinctiveness. If the internal review upholds the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 21 days of the written decision. Applicable appeal filing fees are set out in the Court Fee Regulations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted as a registered-address-only service, provided that a physical Gibraltar address is maintained for service of process and statutory notices. For an exempted limited partnership claiming tax-exempt status, a pure virtual-address arrangement will not satisfy the economic substance evidence requirement; the ELP must demonstrate local management decision-making, Gibraltar-based governance documentation and supervised compliance oversight, even where technical operations are remotely hosted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium_Low: approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced registered-office or subsistence inspection by the Registrar or GFSC for a low-risk remote software and IoT telemetry entity. The probability rises to approximately 40% if PEP involvement, adverse screening flags, or unusual high-risk jurisdiction fund flows are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2014 (Cap. 262) of Gibraltar, as amended, Sections 3-18 (Registration), Section 27 (Exempted Limited Partnership status); Income Tax Act 2010, Sections 44-46 (territorial taxation and exempt partner treatment)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registry of Companies), Office of the Registrar of Companies, 55 Main Street, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ELP-1 — Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership (Registration Statement and Statement of Particulars)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No prescribed minimum paid-up capital for Exempted Limited Partnerships; capital contributions must be quantified in the Partnership Agreement, fully sourced from verifiable funds, and remitted proportionately upon operational activation. No statutory escrow account is mandated by the Limited Partnerships Act 2014, but the licensed Corporate Services Provider must conduct source-of-funds due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the proposed Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement is approved, adopted and authenticated as the constitutive instrument of the Partnership; (2) the General Partner's subscription for a 100% management interest and each Limited Partner's capital contribution schedule in the schedule attached are approved; (3) the registered office at [Registered Office Address, Gibraltar], as notified by the licensed Corporate Services Provider, is adopted as the sole statutory seat; (4) [Name] is appointed General Partner with exclusive management authority; (5) [Name] is appointed Company Secretary and Registered Agent; and (6) the General Partner is authorized to execute all registrations, returns and exempt-status filings with the Gibraltar Companies House and Commissioner of Income Tax.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Exempted Limited Partnership Eligibility Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registry of Companies), Companies Name Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two ranked name alternatives via the Gibraltar Companies House e-portal; verify absence of identical or confusingly similar registered names, trademarks, and prohibited words; obtain non-binding eligibility clearance for the Exempted Limited Partnership designation, including a preliminary determination that the partnership will derive no Gibraltar-source income and may qualify for exempt partner treatment.
required_dossiers: Brief business plan for ISIC 6201 remote support software
KYC/AML identification pack of the proposed General Partner
Declaration of intended non-Gibraltar source of income
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or offensiveness, resubmit an alternative within 3 business days; if exempt status pre-clearance is refused, redraft business plan to eliminate any Gibraltar-resident customer contracting and reapply with a legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Corporate Services Provider and Notary Public, Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed CSP to draft the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement in accordance with the Limited Partnerships Act 2014. The agreement must define profit-sharing ratios, capital contribution schedules, General Partner management authority, limited partner liability caps, withdrawal and transfer clauses, and dispute resolution. Execute the agreement by all partners; notarization is recommended and will be required if opening banking or EMI accounts with certain institutions.
required_dossiers: Full particulars of General Partner and Limited Partners
Proof of address and identification for all partners
Consent of the registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any partner objects to clauses, convene a partners' vote and execute a supplemental agreement; if notarization is requested by a bank, obtain an apostille from the Gibraltar Supreme Court for foreign partners' signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration with the Gibraltar Registry of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registry of Companies) — Filings Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-1 electronically or physically, attaching the executed Partnership Agreement, the registered office consent, and the General Partner's consent to act. Pay the official filing fee of approximately USD 250 (GBP 200). Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Registration, evidencing the Exempted Limited Partnership's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Form ELP-1 (Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership)
Consent of General Partner to act
Identity and verification documents of all general and limited partners
AML due diligence files from the Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, respond within 14 calendar days with corrected particulars; if a background check reveals disqualifying conduct of a proposed General Partner, withdraw that person and appoint a replacement by supplementary resolution before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Exempt Partnership Status Application and Tax Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, submit the Application for Exempt Limited Partnership Status confirming that all income will be derived from outside Gibraltar. Obtain the Certificate of Exempt Status, which fixes the partnership's annual exempt duty (currently GBP 225 indexed) and confirms pass-through treatment so that no Gibraltar corporation tax applies on foreign-source profits. Register each partner with issued Gibraltar tax reference numbers.
required_dossiers: Application for Exempt Limited Partnership Status (Form ELP-2)
Certificate of Registration from the Registry of Companies
Identity and tax residency proofs of all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If exemption is refused, restructure the revenue contracts to eliminate Gibraltar nexus and resubmit; alternatively, accept the standard 12.5% corporate tax rate on any Gibraltar-source profits and amend the Partnership Agreement taxation clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Activation — Payment Rail Onboarding and Data Protection Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) and licensed EMI/PSP onboarding officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the partnership's operational infrastructure by (a) opening a settlement account with a Gibraltar-regulated EMI or licensed payment institution to accommodate SaaS payout rails via Stripe and Paddle; (b) appointing a resident Registered Agent for service of process; and (c) filing, if applicable, notification of personal data processing with the GRA under the Data Protection Act 2019 (GDPR-equivalent). Procure a standard platform-liability insurance certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred EMI declines onboarding due to partnership structure, escalate to the GRA-approved alternative EMI bank (e.g., regulated Gibraltar private bank) with enhanced KYC; if GDPR registration is required, appoint a EU/EEA representative if selling into the European Economic Area.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) — Telecommunications and Data Protection Unit; monitoring oversight only, no industrial manufacturing or operational license is applicable to pure software services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software is a pure-play digital service under ISIC 6201; no physical manufacturing, import/export, or telecommunications operations license is mandated. Optional GRA data protection registration is recommended.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (Gibraltar Environmental Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt — zero physical project; no EIA screening, scoping, or environmental permit required for a remote software business with no premises other than a serviced registered office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste streams; de minimis office e-waste shall be recycled under the Gibraltar WEEE (Charges and Regulations) Act 2018 for IT equipment at the registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no public-facing premises, no structural load, and no workplace occupancy beyond a serviced registered office; the landlord's fire safety certificate and occupant liability insurance covering the registered office suite shall be retained on file. All engineering personnel operate remotely under home-office safety guidelines, imposing no physical clearance obligation on the Partnership.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office (ITO), HM Government of Gibraltar, 231 Main Street, Gibraltar GX11 1AA; electronic services and registration portal: https://egov.gibraltar.gov.gi. Indirect tax and export controls are administered separately by HM Customs of Gibraltar (Gibraltar Customs & Excise), with digital filing through the Gibraltar Customs Single Window (GCSW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Limited Partnerships Act 2016 by filing the partnership statement, appointing a Gibraltar-resident registered office and, where required by the Act, a Gibraltar-resident general partner or licensed manager. Step 2: The Companies Registry automatically transmits the incorporation record to the Income Tax Office, which opens a partnership tax file without a separate application and issues a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) to the ELP; the TRN notice is served on the registered office. Step 3: Each non-resident limited partner must submit the ITO 'Non-Resident Partner Registration Form' together with certified constitutional documents, partnership agreement extract, foreign tax identification number, and identity/beneficial-ownership verification to obtain a partner-specific TRN. Step 4: Where the ELP makes any taxable supplies in Gibraltar, or supplies digital services to Gibraltar consumers, apply to HM Customs of Gibraltar for a Gibraltar VAT registration number; non-resident suppliers must register from the first supply without relying on the ordinary turnover threshold. Step 5: Appoint a Gibraltar tax agent if the ELP has no place of management in Gibraltar, execute the required power of attorney, and complete all subsequent filings through the egov.gibraltar.gov.gi portal. Typical processing: TRN auto-issued within 2-5 working days of incorporation; VAT registration processed in 10-15 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The ELP is fiscally transparent for Gibraltar income tax purposes under the Income Tax Act 2010: no entity-level taxation is imposed on the partnership; each partner is assessed on their agreed share of the partnership profits. Gibraltar-resident partners are taxable on their worldwide share at the applicable individual (up to 28%) or corporate (standard 10%-12.5%) rates, subject to the OECD Pillar Two 15% top-up for in-scope multinational groups. Non-resident partners are taxable in Gibraltar only on Gibraltar-source income or profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment. The ELP itself is not a Gibraltar tax resident unless its central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar; the default offshore management profile of the ELP therefore supports pass-through treatment with no Gibraltar entity-level charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. Available elections and statutory mechanisms for the ELP: (a) default partnership transparency election, with the partnership required to file an annual partner allocation return; (b) an election, made with the Commissioner's consent, for the ELP to be taxed as an assessable company where the arrangement displays corporateness, subject to the Income Tax Act 2010 provisions on 'partnerships treated as companies'; (c) an election under the Income Tax (Exemptions) Regulations for a qualifying private investment fund or certified fund to exempt non-resident investors' offshore investment income from Gibraltar tax; (d) hybrid mismatch self-declarations and reporting under the Income Tax (Hybrid Mismatch) Rules implementing OECD BEPS Action 2, including any reverse-hybrid classification of the ELP where partner jurisdictions diverge; and (e) in respect of US-connected investors, supplementary US Form 8832 classification elections coordinated with the Gibraltar 'reverse hybrid' declaration; the ELP may also elect into the UK 'surrounding territory' treatment only to the extent a UK permanent establishment is created, which is not anticipated under the remote screen-share/IoT delivery model.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Gibraltar VAT) administered under the Value Added Tax Act 2019 and subordinate Orders, structurally aligned with UK VAT principles but constituting an independent fiscal regime; Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT area and outside the EU VAT territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP 100,000 (Gibraltar Pound at parity with GBP; approximately USD 125,000) in taxable turnover in any rolling 12-month period for suppliers established in Gibraltar. No threshold applies to non-established suppliers of digital, electronic, and IoT telemetry services to private consumers in Gibraltar: such suppliers must register from the first supply. Supplies of exported remote screen-share and unattended-device telemetry services fall outside the Gibraltar VAT charge and do not count toward the registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not operate a real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing clearance regime; there is no fiscal digital stamping, no SI-SII-equivalent API, and no mandatory government-cleared e-invoice exchange. However: (i) all VAT invoices issued by a Gibraltar-registered supplier must contain the statutory VAT invoice elements prescribed under the Value Added Tax Act 2019; (ii) cross-border B2B e-invoices should conform to PEPPOL BIS 3.0 to ensure interoperability with buyer-side fiscal systems; (iii) customs export declarations for any physical telemetry hardware, gateways, or screen-sync dongles must be filed electronically via the Gibraltar Customs Single Window, utilising the electronic export declaration (SAD/EAD) with AES-style messaging; and (iv) for pure digital services, the ELP must retain machine-readable delivery logs, IP-geolocation evidence, session timestamps, and Merchant of Record (Stripe/Paddle) transactional APIs as the functional substitute for physical clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating or outside-scope treatment applies as follows: (a) goods: physical telemetry devices, routers, and pre-configured IoT gateways exported from Gibraltar are zero-rated upon removal from Gibraltar territory evidenced by an electronic customs export declaration; (b) B2B services: supplies of remote desktop access and unattended-machine telemetry software to business customers belong where the recipient is established under place-of-supply rules aligned with EU VAT Article 44, so no Gibraltar VAT arises; (c) B2C electronic services: supplies to consumers outside Gibraltar fall outside the Gibraltar VAT charge, with any foreign VAT (EU OSS/IOSS, UK VAT, or non-EU sales tax) administered by Stripe or Paddle as Merchant of Record; and (d) input VAT recovery: recoverable only to the extent attributable to taxable local activities; no Gibraltar VAT refund arises on exports because exports are not charged to Gibraltar VAT. Claims must evidence the recipient's VAT/TIN status, the delivery and performance location through telemetry and session logs, and the absence of any Gibraltar-based personnel or fixed establishment involved in performance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EAD) filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs Single Window, with unique export consignment reference, for physical telemetry gateways, routers, dongles, and pre-provisioned IoT hardware
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (original or electronic telex release) evidencing physical removal from Gibraltar for any goods component
Inward Remittance Certificate in the name of the ELP or original FX settlement statement from the receiving bank/EMI evidencing export consideration credited within the statutory repatriation window
Commercial Invoice in the name of the ELP reflecting Incoterms, HS/CN codes, ISIC 6201 activity description, and SOC code
B2B export contract or master subscription agreement together with the customer's VAT registration number, GSTIN, or equivalent tax identification certificate

Machine-verifiable service delivery log: timestamped remote desktop access session records, unattended-device telemetry manifests, IP-address geolocation data, and edge-node usage reports substantiating the export of digital services
Merchant of Record settlement reports from Stripe and Paddle reconciling each transaction, platform fees, and any VAT/GST collected on behalf of the ELP
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Customs of Gibraltar and the Income Tax Office may audit zero-rating and outside-scope claims for up to six years from the end of the relevant accounting period, extended to twenty years in cases of fraud, wilful default, or careless conduct. Unsupported or contrived zero-rating claims trigger: (a) immediate assessment of Gibraltar VAT at the 10% standard rate with statutory interest from the date of supply; (b) civil penalties of up to 100% of the VAT undercharged, mitigated only by prompt voluntary disclosure under the Civil Penalty Regulations; (c) criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion of VAT under the Value Added Tax Act 2019 and the Criminal Procedure Act, carrying unlimited fines and imprisonment; (d) retrospective clawback of input VAT previously recovered in respect of the related overheads; and (e) reclassification risk whereby the Income Tax Office disregards the ELP's pass-through status if the 'export' structure is found to be a sham, with consequential cross-reporting to UK HMRC and the partners' home tax authorities under the exchange of information framework.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar - Commissioner of Currency (GIP currency issuance); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (banking supervision and AML/CFT oversight); Bank of England (monetary anchor via GIP:GBP 1:1 parity and lender of last resort access via UK clearing relationships)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar imposes no exchange-control legislation and maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at 1:1 to GBP and circulates alongside Bank of England notes, eliminating fiat convertibility friction for GBP-settled flows. Profit remittance, partner distributions, and capital repatriation to non-resident partners are unrestricted and require no central-bank licence or exchange-control approval. USD and EUR conversions are executed freely through licensed banks at market rates; the only practical hurdle is standard AML source-of-funds documentation for large outward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender period, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline applies to export or software-licensing proceeds. Receipts from ISIC 6201 remote-access licensing may be retained indefinitely in original currency (USD, EUR, GBP) or converted at the entity's discretion. No authorised-dealer confirmation or central-bank notification is required; only normal reporting thresholds under the GFSC AML/CFT framework and UK-sanctions screening apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium - UK and EU electronic-money institutions cannot passport into Gibraltar post-Brexit; only GFSC-authorised payment institutions may hold local customer funds. Cross-border EMIs (Airwallex, Wise Business, Revolut Business, neobanking platforms) may on-board the ELP on a bilateral merchant-customer basis for auxiliary disbursements and FX conversion, but they are not substitutes for a GFSC-licensed deposit-taking bank and present counterparty concentration risk. The target rails Stripe and Paddle operate as foreign merchant acquirers / merchants of record, not Gibraltar EMIs; both accept Gibraltar-registered software businesses subject to standard scheme rules, PCI DSS, and enhanced KYC on aggregate payout flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote onboarding is viable at most Gibraltar banks for a Low_Risk_Standard pure-software ELP. Standard protocol: certified copies of the partnership deed, certificate of registration, beneficial-ownership register, apostilled/notarised ID for the general partner and any limited partner above 25%, plus a live video-conference interview with the authorised signatory. Physical in-branch interview is mandatory only at Banco de Sabadell for structures with all non-resident corporate partners; Gibraltar International Bank and Jyske Bank accept fully remote completion when the entity has a verifiable website, active product telemetry, and a UK-resident compliance contact. Lombard Odier requires an existing private-banking relationship and in-person or long-standing referral onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through ELP with non-resident or corporate limited partners creating beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register extract; complete limited partnership agreement and private partnership deed; identity, source-of-funds, and source-of-wealth documentation for each partner holding 25% or more or any general partner; group structure chart; US check-the-box or GBR transparency election where applicable; independent legal opinion confirming partnership law status under Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote card-not-present software sales with high-volume, low-ticket recurring receipts via Stripe and Paddle merchant-of-record payouts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS subscription and end-user licence agreements; Stripe and Paddle merchant-of-record agreements and payout schedules; 12-month pro-forma revenue and transaction-volume model; PCI DSS v4.0 attestation of compliance; live website and secure remote-support portal demonstrating bona fide unattended machine access; refund, chargeback, and fraud-monitoring policies; card-scheme acceptance confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border vendor disbursements to non-EU IOT infrastructure and telemetry suppliers (US, Israel, Taiwan, Cyprus) triggering correspondent-bank sanctions and trade-screening review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor invoices, procurement contracts, and support agreements with clear beneficial beneficiary identification; payment schedule consistent with business plan; partner capital and profit-sharing computation ledger; annual audited financial statements or independent accountant's review; intercompany transfer-pricing file where distributor or licensing affiliates are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use and cybersecurity sensitivity of remote screen-access and unattended machine telemetry software (ISIC 6201) causing financial-crime or export-control red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export-control classification letter from a qualified consultant (EAR99 / UK open-general licence status); acceptable-use policy and prohibited-jurisdiction restrictions; software bill of materials and security attestation (iso/iec 27001 posture or SBOM); contractual prohibition of unlawful surveillance, credential theft, and data exfiltration; end-customer onboarding sample demonstrating legitimate IT-support use consistent with Low_Risk_Standard rating.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital injections must arrive by SWIFT MT103 (USD/EUR/GBP) or UK CHAPS for same-day GBP, referencing the ELP's bank account and a clear purpose description, e.g. 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - LIMITED PARTNERSHIP' or 'LP CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION'; where the bank's systems require a regulatory purpose code, use the BoP capital-transfer class (e.g. 'M03' equity investment) while the free-text field should name the ELP. Standard documentary pack for any single injection over GBP 250,000 or USD 350,000: general-partner resolution/capital call, executed subscription form, source-of-funds briefing, and identity confirmation of the remitting partner. SEPA is not a native Gibraltar rail; EUR injections are cleared via TARGET2 through the bank's EU correspondent, while USD is cleared via the bank's New York correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary correspondent-cleared invoices; MT700 documentary letters of credit are recommended for procurement contracts above GBP 100,000 to add payment certainty for IOT hardware/telemetry suppliers; UK Faster Payments or CHAPS is available for same-day GBP vendor payments via the bank's UK agency arrangement; USD vendor payments via ACH or Fedwire through US correspondents; EUR payments via SEPA/TARGET2 where the counterpart is in the EEA. No Gibraltar exchange-control approval is triggered on any outbound payment. Stripe and Paddle remit aggregate net revenue via non-negotiable MT103 or ACH transfers from their merchant-of-record treasury entities; remittance advice should separately state gross subscription, platform fees, and VAT/GST rows to permit compliant seller-of-record and VAT accounting by the ELP.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: GBP/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (tenors up to 12 months) with Gibraltar-licensed or UK clearing banks
EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards and FX swaps for hedging Paddle EUR subscription settlements and EU IOT supplier costs
Vanilla over-the-counter GBP/USD and GBP/EUR FX options under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or short-form FX master agreement with margin support
GBP/USD cross-currency swaps restricted to matched long-term partner capital injections or qualifying debt refinancing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Return / Annual Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 28 days after the anniversary of registration of the ELP; the registered agent may seek prior Registrar approval to align the return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate from GBP 50 to GBP 500; continued default exposes the ELP to publication of notice in the Gibraltar Gazette and administrative strike-off/deregistration approximately two to three months after the Gazette notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies / Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Central Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the Annual Return within 28 days after the anniversary; any transfer of a limited partnership interest must be updated within 14 days of the relevant transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep or confirm beneficial-ownership records may result in civil penalty up to GBP 1,000 per offence, criminal fines and possible disqualification of the general partner; persistent default can also preclude a Certificate of Good Standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed no later than the return date specified in the annual assessment notice; for a calendar-year ELP, the practical matched deadline is the following 30 June, or within 30 days of a specified Commissioner notice if earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return action by the Income Tax Office includes automatic fixed penalties, daily default penalties, estimated assessment, interest on unpaid tax and court collection proceedings; non-filing may be prosecuted and may jeopardise the ELP's tax-good-standing status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act. An independent audit is mandatory only where the ELP is licensed or regulated by GFSC, acts as a collective investment scheme, is required by the partnership agreement/investment mandate, or is required by a lender or investor; Gibraltar's company law turnover/balance-sheet thresholds may be used by the general partner as practical benchmarks when such an audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Gibraltar, with UK GAAP/FRS 101 equivalents permitted in the general partner's accounting policy; IFRS 9/15 are followed for revenue recognition from the remote screen-share subscription business. Accounts are prepared for partner and tax purposes and are not publicly filed for an ELP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The General Partner must perform an annual review of limited partnership interests and beneficial ownership before the Annual Return date, using the register-book audit procedure carried out by the Gibraltar registered agent. Each transferred partnership interest must be supported by instrument of transfer and recorded in the Register of Limited Partners within 14 days; changes in ultimate beneficial ownership must be recorded in the UBO Register and certified in the annual confirmation delivered to the Registrar. The registered agent must physically inspect all statutory registers at the Gibraltar registered office at least once per year and issue an internal register-audit certificate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Members of a Corporate General Partner (if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - 3,500 per annum for registered office, registered agent, AML/KYC refresher, annual return preparation and register-book maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute in the normal low-risk ELP; if triggered by GFSC, lender or investor requirements, a Gibraltar certified audit generally ranges from USD 5,000 to 10,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% corporate income tax rate applies to Gibraltar-resident companies; the Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) is fiscally transparent and is not itself assessed as a corporation unless separately registered as a company under the Companies Act.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction is available. The ELP's effective tax advantage arises from fiscal transparency and territoriality: non-resident partners are assessable in Gibraltar only on income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar and, for resident partners, foreign income actually remitted to Gibraltar. A remote screen-share/IoT software business invoiced and operated outside Gibraltar may therefore bear no Gibraltar corporate tax, but this result depends on demonstrable substance and source facts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Income Tax Office annual Company/Partnership Tax Return (Form CT-01, with Partnership Schedule P-01 for the ELP) filed through the H.M. Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-services portal or by the official paper form submitted to the Commissioner of Income Tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be delivered within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory default date is 31 December of the following tax year unless an extension is granted by the Commissioner before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reference and legal form: Gibraltar company/partnership registration number, registered office, principal place of business, and jurisdiction of central management and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ELP reference code and identify each partner in the non-resident schedule; do not use a UK or other foreign tax reference unless the partner is itself tax resident there.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates, including any approved change in accounting reference date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the actual ELP fiscal period; a change of partners does not alter the period absent a formal election with the Commissioner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar, plus foreign income remitted to Gibraltar, computed under Income Tax Act source rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remote desktop software and unattended telemetry subscription fees collected through Stripe/Paddle will be treated as foreign-source if the sales activity, server/decision management and substantive operations are outside Gibraltar; no assumption of exemption is permitted without a contemporaneous source analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses and deductions: cloud infrastructure, hosting, third-party software, contractor fees, legal compliance, payment processor fees and office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border related-party charges must be documented, arm's length, and supported by valid invoices; expenses allocated to a connected Cayman/Gibraltar holding structure without business purpose will be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net chargeable income or tax loss; allocation of profit/loss to each partner at their agreed percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner with no Gibraltar-source or remitted income, the allocated income remains outside Gibraltar charge; for a UK-resident partner, HMRC will tax the allocation under UK law, and the ELP should not assert confidentiality against lawful tax exchange.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation at 12.5% where the responsible person is a Gibraltar-resident company; for the ELP, the computation shows each partner's assessable share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all partners are non-resident and no Gibraltar-source/remitted income exists, the return should state nil chargeable income and include the basis, rather than being suppressed entirely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for tax treaty relief, double taxation credit, or exemption where an applicable arrangement exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a current certificate of tax residence for each partner claiming relief; complete the foreign state's applicable WHT form and send it to the payer before payment to obtain relief at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by a general partner or director of the corporate general partner, confirming accurate and complete disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident authorised signatory must hold power of attorney; knowingly making a false declaration is a criminal offence and removes any protection normally afforded by the ELP's limited liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic penalty up to GIP 1,000; continuing daily penalty up to GIP 100 per day; tax-geared penalty up to 100% of the tax due; statutory interest on unpaid tax; estimated assessments may be issued and enforcement includes attachment, director disqualification and, in cases of deliberate default, criminal prosecution.
